finding.expected: Separate supported-family candidate discovery/ambiguity detection from the immutable proof set used by the selected family. Preserve the existing FAILURE proof identity and drift behavior exactly while still rejecting a competing reviewed preservation ref for the same local HEAD. Recheck only evidence relevant to the selected preservation family plus the bounded local-HEAD ambiguity condition, rather than binding unrelated review refs repository-wide. Add deterministic regression proving an unrelated review ref may move without changing the old FAILURE reconciliation result, while a new competing review ref at the exact local HEAD still fails closed. Do not weaken reviewed-Result identity, mutation-edge reproof, or any existing H1R safety gate.
finding.issue: TASK-264 adds refs/heads/aios/review/* to the global preservation snapshot and folds that entire mapping into expected_proof for both reviewed-Result and existing FAILURE reconciliation. On the FAILURE path, movement of any unrelated review ref anywhere in the repository between proof checks now causes canonical reconciliation proof drift, even though the failed candidate, failure/failure-artifacts identity, upstream target, worktree and local history are unchanged. Before TASK-264, unrelated review refs were not part of FAILURE preservation identity. This violates the hard constraint and AC2 requirement that the existing H1R FAILURE-preservation path remain behaviorally unchanged.

original_constraints: Keep the existing H1R FAILURE-preservation path behaviorally unchanged, including its canonical failure/failure-artifacts proof, drift checks, complete local-only reachability proof, worktree/index/submodule/ignored-path checks, exact-target reset, postconditions and restart-generation safety.

Reviewed-result preservation must validate the exact canonical task/run/result/review identity and candidate SHA using existing artifact/review semantics; the canonical review decision must be the unique exact decision for that RUN, bind reviewed_sha to local HEAD, and have verdict PASS. Missing, malformed, conflicting, moved, ambiguous, cross-task, non-PASS or substituted transport must fail closed rather than falling back to another preservation class.

All local-only commits that would become unreachable from local main after reset must remain reachable from the exact validated reviewed candidate preservation identity, and that identity plus canonical target/upstream/worktree safety must be rechecked at the destructive mutation edge.

Preservation-family selection must be deterministic and closed: exactly one valid supported preservation proof may authorize reconciliation; zero, multiple, conflicting or mixed ambiguous proofs fail closed without resetting or creating a RUN.

The observed RUN-262-004-shaped regression must prove reviewed PASS Result preservation can recover a diverged local main while negative regressions prove an unreviewed candidate, non-PASS/mismatched review decision, missing/substituted artifacts, ambiguous preservation and moved proof remain non-destructive.
